sentences.text: Edith Marsh is the person being assessed.
Care assessor Janet Fielding is from the council.
The assessment is happening because the care assessor is seeking to understand the person's needs at home.
Pauline Reid is a neighbour who is present during the assessment.
Edith uses a frame to get about.
Edith does not go upstairs.
Gary brought Edith's bed down to the front room.
Gary is Edith's son and lives with her.
Gary works at a garage on Station Road.
Gary works from eight to six, sometimes later.
Gary helps Edith with shopping, getting up, and taking her tablets.
Edith can mostly get to the toilet herself.
Edith uses a commode and wears pads when she is not quick enough.
Gary changes Edith's pad when he is home; otherwise, Edith manages it herself.
Edith is alone during the day when Gary is at work.
Gary leaves work around half past seven.
Gary sometimes does not return until nine o'clock.
Pauline Reid visits Edith most afternoons.
Pauline says Edith is left in wet clothes most days, with wet pads and skirts, when she visits at two.
Pauline says Edith is left in wet clothes on four or five days a week.
Pauline helps Edith change when she is willing.
Gary leaves Edith a sandwich for lunch usually.
There is no food in the fridge on the days Pauline has checked, with only a small amount of milk that has gone off.
Pauline says the fridge has been empty three or four times in the last few weeks.
Gary puts Edith's tablets out in a box.
The tablet box is on the side of the house.
Edith has not had her tablets for a week, with the box full since Tuesday the 17th.
Edith says she forgets to take her tablets and that Gary is busy.
Edith denies that Gary or anyone has ever hit her or hurt her.
Pauline denies seeing any signs of harm or abuse.
